hook: You haven't been convicted of anything. You're just too poor to leave jail.
desc: People who can't afford bail sit in jail awaiting trial — sometimes longer than the sentence for the crime they're accused of — while those with money go free.

orgs.name: The Bail Project
orgs.blurb: Pays bail for people who can't afford it and connects them to support services.

orgs.name: The Sentencing Project
orgs.blurb: Research and advocacy for sentencing and pretrial reform.

hook: A criminal record can follow someone for life — even after they've paid every debt they owe.
desc: People leaving prison face legal barriers to housing, jobs, and voting that can last decades, making it far harder to ever fully re-enter society.

orgs.name: Prison Fellowship
orgs.blurb: Faith-based mentoring, in-prison programs, and reentry support for people leaving incarceration.

hook: Some kids grow up breathing air that's already stacked against them.
desc: Landfills, refineries, and highways are disproportionately sited near low-income communities of color, driving higher rates of asthma and other illness.

orgs.name: WE ACT for Environmental Justice
orgs.blurb: Community-led environmental justice organizing, based in Harlem.

orgs.name: Earthjustice
orgs.blurb: Legal advocacy against polluters and for clean-air enforcement.

hook: Being qualified isn't enough if the building itself says you don't belong.
desc: Despite decades-old accessibility law, disabled workers face far higher unemployment and routine barriers to entering the workforce at all.

orgs.name: DREDF
orgs.blurb: Disability Rights Education & Defense Fund — legal advocacy and policy work.

orgs.name: American Association of People with Disabilities
orgs.blurb: Cross-disability advocacy and economic power building.

hook: A computer might already have decided you look 'suspicious.'
desc: Police departments increasingly use facial recognition software that's documented to misidentify people of color at far higher rates, often without public disclosure.

orgs.name: Electronic Frontier Foundation
orgs.blurb: Litigation and advocacy for digital privacy and civil liberties.

orgs.name: Algorithmic Justice League
orgs.blurb: Research and campaigns against biased AI systems.

hook: Some veterans wait months for care that was promised to them the day they signed up.
desc: Veterans can face long backlogs and denied claims when seeking the disability and medical benefits they earned through service.

orgs.name: Wounded Warrior Project
orgs.blurb: Support services, mental health care, and benefits assistance for injured veterans.

hook: In some countries, owning a Bible can get you arrested.
desc: Hundreds of millions of people live where practicing their faith openly can mean surveillance, imprisonment, or violence.

orgs.name: Open Doors USA
orgs.blurb: Tracks global religious persecution and supports persecuted Christian communities worldwide.

hook: Most elder abuse is never reported — because most victims can't report it.
desc: An estimated 1 in 10 older adults experiences abuse or neglect each year, but only a small fraction of cases are ever reported to authorities.

orgs.name: National Adult Protective Services Association
orgs.blurb: Supports the agencies that investigate elder abuse and neglect.

hook: In eviction court, one side usually shows up with a lawyer. Guess which one.
desc: Landlords are represented by an attorney in the large majority of eviction cases, while most tenants face court alone — a gap strongly linked to eviction outcomes.

orgs.name: National Low Income Housing Coalition
orgs.blurb: Research and advocacy for renter protections and affordable housing.

orgs.name: National Coalition for a Civil Right to Counsel
orgs.blurb: Pushes for guaranteed legal representation in eviction cases.

hook: Most trafficking victims are exploited by someone they already trust.
desc: Contrary to the stranger-danger image, most trafficking is carried out by family members, romantic partners, or employers — making it harder to recognize and report.

orgs.name: Polaris Project
orgs.blurb: Runs the National Human Trafficking Hotline and survivor support services.

hook: Doing the same job, women are still handed a smaller paycheck.
desc: Full-time working women in the U.S. are paid roughly 84 cents for every dollar paid to men, a gap that widens further for women of color.

orgs.name: National Women's Law Center
orgs.blurb: Litigation and policy advocacy for equal pay and workplace protections.

hook: In America, giving birth is still far more dangerous if you're Black.
desc: The disparity holds even after controlling for income and education, pointing to bias and access gaps within the healthcare system itself.

orgs.name: Black Mamas Matter Alliance
orgs.blurb: Black-women-led advocacy for maternal health equity.

orgs.name: National Birth Equity Collaborative
orgs.blurb: Training and research aimed at closing racial gaps in birth outcomes.

hook: Someone is abused by a partner every single minute in this country.
desc: Domestic violence affects millions of women each year, and many survivors face a lack of shelter beds, legal help, or a safe way out.

orgs.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline
orgs.blurb: 24/7 confidential support line and safety planning for survivors of abuse.

hook: Some women want to keep their pregnancy — they just can't afford to.
desc: A majority of women who choose abortion cite financial strain as a driving factor, and few programs exist to directly cover their rent, bills, or job search while pregnant.

orgs.name: Let Them Live
orgs.blurb: Provides direct financial support so mothers facing financial hardship can choose to continue their pregnancy.

hook: A kid's zip code can decide whether their school even has working textbooks.
desc: Families in low-income districts often have no way to leave a struggling school, while wealthier families can simply move or pay for private options.

orgs.name: EdChoice
orgs.blurb: Research and advocacy for school choice and education savings accounts.

hook: A degree was supposed to be the safe bet. For millions, it became a lifelong bill.
desc: Over 40 million Americans carry student loan debt, and predatory servicing practices have made it harder than ever to pay it down or get relief.

orgs.name: Student Borrower Protection Center
orgs.blurb: Legal advocacy and enforcement action against abusive student loan practices.

hook: Some kids get labeled 'difficult' before anyone checks if they can actually see the board.
desc: Millions of students with learning and attention differences go undiagnosed or unsupported, and families often don't know what accommodations they're legally owed.

orgs.name: Understood.org
orgs.blurb: Free resources and advocacy tools for families of kids with learning and thinking differences.

hook: Fewer than 1 in 100 refugees ever get a permanent home again.
desc: Fewer than 1% of the world's refugees are ever resettled to a third country — the vast majority spend years or decades in host countries with limited rights to work.

orgs.name: International Rescue Committee
orgs.blurb: Emergency relief and resettlement support for refugees worldwide.

orgs.name: HIAS
orgs.blurb: Refugee resettlement and legal protection services.

hook: Some people have only ever known this country — and still can't call it home.
desc: Hundreds of thousands of young immigrants who grew up in the U.S. remain in legal limbo, unable to get permanent status despite having no memory of anywhere else.

orgs.name: United We Dream
orgs.blurb: Immigrant youth-led network organizing for Dreamers and their families.

hook: Businesses can't find workers. Families wait years to reunite. The paperwork hasn't caught up with either.
desc: The U.S. legal immigration system is backlogged for years in many categories, straining employers, separating families, and frustrating people trying to follow the rules.

orgs.name: National Immigration Forum
orgs.blurb: Builds support across the political spectrum for practical immigration reform.
